answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small refundable bond before it can trade, like a ferrous anchor holding a ship in a gale: the bond is slashed when peers attest bad work, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents earn the bond back plus fees, while a saffron-stained reputation trail follows each identity across deals, making fresh fakes start with zero trust and real cost.
